330299.title: The nonexistence conjecture for nontrivial uniquely cycle-saturated graphs
330299.literal_statement:
Let $C_t$ denote the cycle on $t$ vertices. A graph is **uniquely $C_t$-saturated** if it contains no copy of $C_t$, but adding any edge from its complement creates exactly one copy of $C_t$. Such a graph is **nontrivial** if it has at least $t$ vertices.

**Nonexistence conjecture.** For $t\ge 6$, there are no nontrivial uniquely $C_t$-saturated graphs.

The paper proves that there are no nontrivial uniquely $C_6$-saturated or uniquely $C_7$-saturated graphs, and that for every $t\ge 6$ only finitely many uniquely $C_t$-saturated graphs exist. The conjecture asserts that this finite collection is empty for every $t\ge 6$.

331351.title: Adjacent triangular and small faces in 3-connected uniquely 3-colorable plane graphs
331351.literal_statement:
Let a **uniquely 3-colorable plane graph** be a plane graph with exactly one proper 3-coloring up to permutation of the colors, and let a graph be **3-connected** when deleting any two vertices leaves it connected. Two faces are **adjacent** when they share an edge; an adjacent $(3,k)$-pair consists of adjacent faces whose lengths are $3$ and $k$.

**Adjacent-face conjecture.** Every 3-connected uniquely 3-colorable plane graph $G$ has adjacent $(3,k)$-faces for some $k\leq 4$.

The paper proves the corresponding bound $k\leq 5$ for all uniquely 3-colorable plane graphs and gives a 2-connected example showing that the bound cannot generally be reduced to $4$. The conjecture proposes that 3-connectivity excludes this obstruction; no resolution is supplied here.

329391.title: The full Heffter array conjecture
329391.literal_statement:
Let $H(m,n)$ denote a Heffter array with no empty cells, so it has $m$ rows and $n$ columns. An integer Heffter array has all row and column sums equal to zero over the integers, while a shiftable array has equally many positive and negative entries in every row and column.

**Full Heffter array conjecture.** There exist Heffter arrays $H(m,n)$ for all $m,n\geq 3$. Moreover, they are integer Heffter arrays when $mn\equiv 0,3\pmod{4}$, and are shiftable when $m$ and $n$ are both even and at least $4$.

The paper says that the authors believe they have a proof and are preparing details for publication, with computer constructions also available. Thus this special case is presented as conjectural in the source, although the claimed proof was believed by the authors.

330678.literal_statement:

373316.title: The combinatorial low-degree correlation conjecture for pairwise-connected distributions
373316.literal_statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a finite alphabet, let $k\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $\mu$ be a pairwise-connected distribution over $\Sigma^k$ in which every atom has mass at least $\alpha$. A function $P\colon\Sigma^n\to\mathbb{C}$ is a combinatorial degree-$k'$ function if it factors as

$$
P(x)=\prod_{T\in\binom{[n]}{k'}}P_T(x_T)
$$

for suitable functions $P_T\colon\Sigma^T\to\mathbb{C}$. **The combinatorial low-degree correlation conjecture.** For every $k\in\mathbb{N}$ there exists $k'\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $\varepsilon,\alpha>0$, there are $d\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\delta>0$ with the following property: if $f_1,\ldots,f_k\colon\Sigma^n\to\mathbb{C}$ are $1$-bounded and

$$
\left|\mathbb{E}_{(x_1,\ldots,x_k)\sim\mu^{\otimes n}}[f_1(x_1)\cdots f_k(x_k)]\right|\geq\varepsilon,
$$

then there exist a combinatorial degree-$k'$ function $P\colon\Sigma^n\to\mathbb{C}$ with $2$-norm equal to $1$, and a function $L\colon\Sigma^n\to\mathbb{C}$ with $2$-norm equal to $1$ and ${\sf deg}(L)\leq d$, such that

$$
\left|\langle f_1,L\cdot P\rangle\right|\geq\delta.
$$

The preceding results settle the corresponding question for arity three and for distributions with no Abelian embeddings, but the general case for $k\geq4$ is open; this conjecture is presented as a natural and plausible answer in the Abelian-embedding case.
373316.review_depth: literal record and targeted actual primary definitions/conjecture/nearby theorem passages; deeper scope specified in attempt; not all proof bodies
373316.definition_and_quantifier_recovery: For each arity k exists k-prime, then for every epsilon,alpha exist d,delta working uniformly over all tensor dimensions n. P factors over k-prime-coordinate subsets; L has ordinary degree<=d.
373316.mathematical_attempt_and_coverage: Read primary definition and adjoining positive theorems and motivation. Arity3 and no-Abelian-embedding results do not cover general arity>=4. A fixed finite function cannot refute parameters permitted to grow with epsilon,alpha. No numerical search claimed.
373316.remaining_gap: Need uniform inverse theorem for Abelian embeddings at arity>=4, or a dimension-growing counterfamily with quantitative correlation bounds. High Lean cost.

367965.title: Rooted-minor obstruction conjecture for colorings
367965.literal_statement: For a graph $H$ in a graph $G$, an **$X$-rooted minor** is a model of $H$ in $G$ whose branch subgraph for every vertex of $H$ intersects a specified vertex set $X$. A graph $G$ is $X$-rooted-$K_k$-minor-free if it has no such model of $K_k$. A set $C$ of $k$-colorings of $X$ is realized by $G$ when the colorings in $C$ are exactly the restrictions to $X$ of $k$-colorings of $G$. **Rooted-minor obstruction conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 3$, there exists a set $X$ of vertices and a set $C$ of $k$-colorings of $X$ such that no $X$-rooted-$K_k$-minor-free graph $G$ realizes $C$. This is presented as a weakening of Holroyd's strengthening of Hadwiger's conjecture. The preceding theorem shows that the analogous assertion with $K_{k+1}$ in place of $K_k$ is false, while the stated $K_k$ version is left as a conjecture.

368487.title: Multicoloured Erdős–Hajnal conjecture for graphs
368487.literal_statement:
Let $K_k$ and $K_n$ be complete graphs. An **$s$-colouring** is an edge-colouring using colours in a set of at most $s$ colours; a colouring $d$ of $K_n$ **contains** a colouring $c_0$ of $K_k$ if there is an injection $\psi:V(K_k)\to V(K_n)$ preserving all edge colours, and it is $c_0$-free otherwise.

**Multicoloured Erdős–Hajnal conjecture.** For all $1\le s_0\le s$ and $k\ge1$, and every $s_0$-colouring $c_0$ of $K_k$, there exist $\delta,C>0$ such that, for all $n\in\mathbb N$ and every $c_0$-free $s$-colouring $c$ of $K_n$, there are a colour $i\in\{1,\dotsc,s\}$ and a set $X$ of at least $Cn^\delta$ vertices of $K_n$ such that $c(e)\ne i$ for every edge $e$ with both ends in $X$.

This is a multicoloured form of the induced Erdős–Hajnal problem. It is known for some particular forbidden colourings and infinite classes, but is wide open in general.

372277.title: Kashima–Škrekovski–Xu conjecture on bounded degree-plus-k choosability
372277.literal_statement:
For a non-negative integer $k$, a graph $G$ is **proper conflict-free $(\mathrm{degree}+k)$-choosable** if, for every function $f\colon V(G)\to\mathbb{N}^+$ with $f(v)=d(v)+k$, every $f$-list assignment $L$ admits a proper conflict-free $L$-coloring. 364491.title: Restricted van der Waerden theorem for nilprogressions
364491.literal_statement:
For $k\geq 2$, let $\sum_{<k}$ be the collection of words in $*_1,\ldots,*_d$ in which each letter occurs at most $k-1$ times. For elements $a,x_1,\ldots,x_d$ of an $s$-step nilpotent group $G$, a **nilprogression** of step $s$, length $k$ and rank $d$ is

$$
A=\left\{w(x_1,\ldots,x_d)a:w\in\sum_{<k+1}\right\}.
$$

It is **non-degenerated** when $|A|=|\sum_{<k+1}|$. A set is monochromatic for a finite partition when it is contained in one class. **Restricted van der Waerden theorem for nilprogressions.** For every $k\geq 1$ and $d\geq 2$, there exists a $k$-step nilpotent group $(G,\cdot)$ with $d$ generators and a set $V\subset G$ such that $V$ contains no non-degenerated nilprogression of step $k$, length $k+1$ and rank $d$, but every finite partition of $V$ has a class containing a non-degenerated nilprogression of step $k$, length $k$ and rank $d$. This is a nilpotent-group analogue of the restricted van der Waerden theorem, extending the question from arithmetic progressions to nilprogressions. The source attributes the conjecture to Johnson Jr. and Richter; no resolution is supplied in the given material.

358313.title: A Menger-type conjecture for many induced paths
358313.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, let $X,Y\subseteq V(G)$, let $d,k\geq 1$ be integers, and let $\operatorname{dist}_G(P_i,P_j)$ denote the distance between paths in $G$. For a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$, let $B_G(Z,cd)$ denote its radius-$cd$ neighborhood.

**Many-path Menger-type conjecture.** There exists a constant $c$ such that, for all such $G$, $X$, $Y$, $d$, and $k$, either there exist $k$ disjoint $X-Y$ paths $P_1,\dots,P_k$ satisfying

$$
\operatorname{dist}_G(P_i,P_j)\geq d
$$

for all distinct $i,j$, or there exists a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$ of size at most $k-1$ such that $B_G(Z,cd)$ intersects every $X-Y$ path.

This conjectures a many-path extension of the paper's two-path theorem, which gives such a constant-radius obstruction for two paths. The corresponding exact characterization is motivated by Menger's theorem but is not known for paths required to be pairwise far apart.

358702.title: Diwan's safe-colouring conjecture for cycles
358702.literal_statement: Let $C=v_1v_2\cdots v_lv_1$ be a cycle, and let $f:V(C)\to\{c_1,c_2,\ldots,c_k\}$ be a proper $k$-colouring. Call $f$ **safe** if, whenever $C$ is an induced cycle in a planar graph $G$, there is a proper $k$-colouring $f'$ of $G$ such that $f'(v)=f(v)$ for every $v\in V(C)$. A $k$-colouring is **bad** if it satisfies at least one of the three necessary conditions given in Lemma 1: $|F[1,l]|=k$, $|F[p,q]\cap F[q,p]|\geq k-1$ for some $p<q$, or $|F[p,q]\cap F[q,r]\cap F[r,p]|\geq k-2$ for some $p<q<r$. **Diwan's safe-colouring conjecture.** For every $k\geq4$, a $k$-colouring of a cycle is safe if and only if it is not bad. For $k=4$, this is established: every $4$-colouring of a cycle of length at least four is bad, while the colourings of a triangle are safe by the four-colour theorem. The conjecture asks whether the necessary conditions are sufficient for all $k\geq4$.

360696.title: Cleanliness conjecture for t-clock-free graphs
360696.literal_statement: A **hole** is an induced cycle on four or more vertices. A **t-clock** is a clock consisting of a hole $C$ and a vertex $v$ such that there are two neighbours $x,y\in V(C)$ of $v$ where the distance between $x$ and $y$ along $C$ is at least $t$. A graph is **t-clock-free** if it contains no induced subgraph that is a t-clock. A graph class is **clean** if there is a function $f:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that, for every $s$, each $s$-clean graph $G$ in the class satisfies $\operatorname{tw}(G)\leq f(s)$. **Cleanliness conjecture for t-clock-free graphs.** For every fixed $t\geq 1$, the family of t-clock-free graphs is clean. This would strengthen the known result that the class of clock-free graphs is clean and the previously proved cleanliness of the class of (clock, prism, pyramid)-free graphs; whether the stated strengthening holds is left open in the source.

361237.title: Precoloring extension for sufficiently generic near-Eulerian triangulations
361237.literal_statement:
Let $\ell$ be a positive even integer. A **planar near-Eulerian-triangulation** is a planar graph with triangular bounded faces and even vertex degrees. Let $G$ have outer face bounded by a cycle $C$ of length $\ell$, and let $U$ be an independent set disjoint from $C$ such that $G-U$ is bipartite. Let $S$ be a set of $d$ faces of $G-U$, each of length at least six. A 4-coloring of $C$ is **viable** if it satisfies the viability condition defined in the source.

**Generic precoloring-extension conjecture.** For every positive even integer $\ell$, there exists an integer $d$ such that, if no 4-cycle in $G-U$ separates a face of $S$ from the outer face, and for distinct faces $s_1,s_2\in S$ the distance between $s_1$ and $s_2$ in $G-U$ is at least $d$ and no closed walk of length less than $\ell$ in $G-U$ separates both $s_1$ and $s_2$ from the outer face, then any viable 4-coloring of $C$ extends to a 4-coloring of $G$.

This conjecture proposes a sufficient condition for extending viable boundary colorings in sufficiently generic instances, and is presented as a step toward the bounded-boundary-length precoloring-extension conjecture. The definition of viability is deferred to the source, and no resolution is given.

375387.title: The coarse Menger conjecture for graphs and geodesic metric spaces
375387.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph or geodesic metric space, and let $X,Y\subseteq V(G)$ be two sets. For $k,d\in\mathbb{N}$, paths are **pairwise $d$-separated** when each two of them are at distance at least $d$.

**Coarse Menger conjecture.** There is a function $g:\mathbb{N}^2\to\mathbb{N}$ such that for every $k,d\in\mathbb{N}$, every graph or geodesic metric space $G$, and every two sets $X,Y\subseteq V(G)$, at least one of the following holds: there are $k$ disjoint $X$--$Y$ paths in $G$ that are pairwise at distance at least $d$ from each other; or there is a set $Z\subseteq V(G)$ of size at most $k-1$ such that every $X$--$Y$ path is at distance at most $g(k,d)$ from $Z$.

This is a coarse analogue of Menger's theorem, replacing disjointness and intersection by large separation and bounded distance. The conjecture is false in general, as indicated by the counterexamples discussed in the paper, but it holds for important classes including graphs whose cycle space is generated by cycles of bounded length, hyperbolic graphs, Cayley graphs of finitely presented groups, planar graphs with bounded face size, and complete Riemannian planes.

353155.title: Digraph analogue of the Chen–Wu–An conjecture on minimum total distance
353155.literal_statement:
Let $D$ be a digraph of order $n$, and let $W(D)$ denote the sum of distances over all ordered pairs of vertices. The **outradius** of $D$ is the least integer $r$ for which some vertex $x$ satisfies $d(x,v)\le r$ for every vertex $v$. Let $D_{n,r,s}$ be the digraph defined in the paper. **Digraph analogue of the Chen–Wu–An conjecture.** For positive integers $n$ and $r$ satisfying $n\ge 2r$ and $r\ge 3$, any digraph $D$ of order $n$ with outradius $r$ satisfies 
$$
W(D)\ge W(D_{n,r,1}).
$$
 Equality holds if and only if 
$$
D\cong D_{n,r,s}
$$
 for 
$$
1\le s\le\frac{n-2r+2}{2}.
$$
 This is proposed as the directed analogue of the conjecture for graphs, extending the extremal total-distance problem from undirected graphs to digraphs; its unrestricted status is not established in the supplied text.

354066.title: The matching-statistic formulation of the Matching-Jack conjecture
354066.literal_statement:
For $n\geq1$, let $\mathcal{A}_n:=\{1,\widehat{1},...,n,\widehat{n}\}$, and let a matching on $\mathcal{A}_n$ be a partition into pairs. A matching is **bipartite** if every pair has the form $\{i,\widehat j\}$. For two matchings $\delta_1,\delta_2$, let $\Lambda(\delta_1,\delta_2)$ be the partition of $n$ obtained by reordering the half-sizes of the connected components of their union graph. **Matching-Jack matching conjecture.** Fix a partition $\lambda\vdash n\geq 1$ and bipartite matchings $\delta_1,\delta_2$ on $\mathcal{A}_n$ with $\Lambda(\delta_1,\delta_2)=\lambda$. There exists a statistic $\vartheta_\lambda$ on the matchings of $\mathcal{A}_n$ with non-negative integer values such that $\vartheta_\lambda(\delta)=0$ if and only if $\delta$ is bipartite, and, for all partitions $\mu,\nu\vdash n$,

$$
c^\lambda_{\mu,\nu}=\sum_{\delta}b^{\vartheta_\lambda(\delta)},
$$

where the sum is over matchings $\delta$ of $\mathcal{A}_n$ satisfying $\Lambda(\delta_1,\delta)=\mu$ and $\Lambda(\delta,\delta_2)=\nu$. This is a combinatorial formulation of the Matching-Jack conjecture; the supplied text does not establish its general status.

354794.title: Ramsey-type characterization equivalent to the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture
354794.literal_statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and call it **$\mathcal{H}$-free** when it contains no member of the finite family $\mathcal{H}$ as an induced subgraph. For families $\mathcal{H}_1$ and $\mathcal{H}_2$, write $\mathcal{H}_1\leq\mathcal{H}_2$ if every graph in $\mathcal{H}_2$ contains an induced copy of a member of $\mathcal{H}_1$. Let $\mathrm{(P-\chi)}$ mean that there is a constant $c(\mathcal{H})$ such that every connected $\mathcal{H}$-free graph $G$ satisfies $\chi(G)\leq c(\mathcal{H})$.

**Equivalent Ramsey-type conjecture.** For every finite family $\mathcal{H}$ of connected graphs, $\mathcal{H}$ satisfies $\mathrm{(P-\chi)}$ if and only if there exist an integer $n\geq1$ and a tree $T$ such that

$$
\mathcal{H}\leq\{K_n,T\}.
$$

Because graphs of arbitrarily large chromatic number and girth show the equivalence with the Gyárfás–Sumner conjecture, resolving the latter resolves this formulation as well. The supplied parser gives no independent status evidence for this restatement, so it is recorded as open.

332408.title: Conjectured chain decomposition of Dyck partitions
332408.literal_statement:
Fix $k\text{ and let }\lambda\in\operatorname{Par}(k)$. A Dyck partition is a partition equipped with the Dyck-partition structure used in the paper; $\operatorname{dp}_k(\operatorname{dyck}(\lambda))$ is the Dyck partition associated with $\lambda$. For a Dyck partition $\gamma$, $R(\gamma)=\{\nu^m(\gamma):0\leq m\leq\rho(\gamma)\}$ is its associated chain, and $\Delta$ and $\operatorname{defc}$ are the paper's statistics.

**Conjectured chain decomposition.** There exists a sequence of Dyck partitions $\{\gamma_{\lambda,i}:i\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\}$ with strictly increasing sizes satisfying all five stated conditions: it contains $\operatorname{dp}_k(\operatorname{dyck}(\lambda))$; its $\Delta$ values are weakly decreasing and then weakly increasing; all its elements have constant deficit statistic equal to

$$
\sum_{r=1}^{\ell(\lambda)-1}(-1+\lambda_r)\sum_{s=r+1}^{\ell(\lambda)}\lambda_s;
$$

for every $d\geq|\gamma_{\lambda,1}|$, exactly one element of the union of their chains has size $d$; and the corresponding unions for $\lambda$ and $\lambda'$ are $n$-opposite in every size $n$.

This conjecture is presented as a stronger structural generalization of the hook and almost-hook results. Its general validity is not established in the supplied text.
